title: From the Camp, to the Cross

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Israelites did so; they sent them outside the camp. They did just as the Lord had instructed Moses. - Num 5:4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This short verse simply records that Israel obeyed — they did "just as the Lord had instructed Moses." Once again, the quiet refrain of obedience runs through the book of Numbers. God spoke, and His people did what He said.

But there is something deeper here that we should not miss. The unclean were sent "outside the camp." That phrase becomes significant as the whole story of Scripture unfolds. To be outside the camp was to be separated, cut off from the place of God's presence and the fellowship of His people.

The New Testament picks up this very phrase and applies it to Jesus. Hebrews tells us that Jesus "suffered outside the city gate" — outside the camp — to make His people holy through His own blood (Heb 13:12). The One who was perfectly clean willingly took the place of the unclean. He went outside so that we could be brought inside.

Think of the wonder of this. In the old covenant, the unclean were sent out. But Jesus, the truly clean and holy One, went out to the place of separation for us. He bore our uncleanness so that we could dwell forever with God.

If you have ever felt like an outsider, unworthy to belong, look to Christ. He went outside the camp so that in Him you would never be shut out again.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Have you ever felt like a spiritual "outsider"?
- How does it move you that Jesus went "outside the camp" for you?
- What does it mean to be brought inside through Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You for going outside the camp, bearing my uncleanness, so that I could be brought near to God. I am home in You. Amen.
